maggie: FYI found a weird perf spike after converting Mixtral-v1 for the dedicated pool, looks like kernel selection went to a slow path.
jordan: ugh, seen screenshots?
maggie: attaching quick logs (snippet below). kernel_choice: fallback_scalar_attention -> latency +2.1x
maggie: ```
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] model=mixtral-v1, sequence=1024, kernel=fast_mha -> OK
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] model=mixtral-v1, sequence=1024, kernel=fallback_scalar_attention, reason=rope_scale_missing
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] perf=ms/step 21.3 -> 45.1
```
sam: rope_scale_missing? HF config missing that field sometimes when conversion strips metadata.
kira: is it the safetensors metadata parity? we had a bug where safetensors header lacked kv/layout flags.
ryan: pinging infra-bot for recent conversion runs @infra-bot
infra-bot: conversion-job-4812 started by maggie. logs: https://ci.redwood/conv/4812 :white_check_mark:
maggie: repro steps: checkout conv-scripts@main, run `python convert.py --src hf://mixtral/v1 --out safetensors --preserve-metadata`
jordan: can you paste the HF config fragment? maybe rope scaling is encoded under transformer.extra or missing by name.
maggie: here's relevant hf config snippet:
```json
{"hidden_size":4096,"num_attention_heads":32,"rope_freq_base":10000}
```
maggie: note there's no explicit `rope_scaling` or `scale_base` fields that our runtime expects.
sam: runtime kernel selector looks for `rope_scaling.type` or `rope_scaling.scale` and falls back when absent -> picks generic slow kernel.
kira: short-term patch: change kernel selector to assume legacy base scaling param if missing. long-term: add conversion check/assertion.
yan: I ran a profiler on the bad run: top time spent in attention kernel (scalar fallback) and a weird KV cache invalidation thrash.
ryan: profile snapshot: ```
CPU: 12% | CUDA: 87%
attn_kernel_scalar: 63% of token time
kv_cache_rewrites: 11% (unexpected per request)
```
maggie: kv cache rewrites? maybe conversion changed the kv dtype layout (channels-last vs default) and runtime writes new layout when reading -> causing copies.
jordan: good catch — we had a metadata flag `kv_storage_format` in safetensors that we recently stopped writing for some models.
kira: action items:
  - add validation to convert.py to ensure rope_scaling keys and kv_storage_format present
  - add runtime guard to prefer fast kernel if inferred rope scale reasonable
  - add a unit test that runs small perf profile on CI (sequence 512/1024)
sam: +1. also add an opt-in batching heuristic tweak: if runtime sees many seqs ~1024, reduce batch size to avoid memory thrash.
ryan: I pushed a tiny kernel-selector change: https://github.com/redwood/rt/commit/abc123 — it infers rope_scale from rope_freq_base if missing. running canary now.
maggie: thanks. I opened a PR for conversion script checks: https://github.com/redwood/tools/pull/92 — includes safetensors metadata write and a failing test that simulates older hf configs.
kira: let's also add an alert: perf-regression classifier should raise when kernel changes from 'fast_mha' -> 'fallback_scalar_attention' in prod.
jordan: agree. And log which config fields were present so we can triage quickly.
maggie: quick workaround deployed to dedicated pool: prefer fast kernel when estimated scaling in [0.9, 1.1] inferred. monitoring :eyes:
infra-bot: canary rollout to dedicated pool: 5% -> 20% -> 100% (in progress)
ryan: after canary, latency back to normal for those requests. still chasing a few outliers where kv_copy spikes.
sam: I'll instrument kv read path to log layout mismatch and size. hopefully narrow down.
kira: great thread. once PRs land, let's schedule a small postmortem note in #postmortems with checklist for model onboarding.
maggie: thanks everyone :pray:
